basis: Hypomyelination, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and dental abnormalities define the syndrome; myopia affects 3/4, with optic atrophy also reported.
Most arise in salivary glands; other origins represent subtypes. Perineural pain alone does not establish common lasting neurologic dysfunction.
Alzheimer disease subtype defined by cerebral neurodegeneration and dementia.
Malignant tumour originates in bone; lung metastases are described, but involvement in at least 30% is not established by the supplied evidence.
Defined by disease of the midbrain.
PEX7 metabolic disorder; neuropathy, retinal dystrophy and cardiomyopathy each reported in 1/1 patient. Hearing loss also 1/1, omitted by cap; evidence is sparse.
Benign neoplasm confined to the vagina, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Sarcoma originates in the skin; individual histologic subtypes do not establish additional axes across the umbrella.
Lysosomal storage disease defined by neurologic dysfunction and retinal abnormalities with visual loss; skeletal and visceral disease chiefly characterize type II.
Nonsyndromic inherited sensorineural hearing loss.
Choroidal leakage causes subretinal fluid and retinal visual dysfunction; local choroidal vessels do not establish systemic cardiovascular disease.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome with developmental delay in 9/10. Joint hypermobility in 4/8 lacks documented damage; overweight alone does not establish endocrine disease.
Toxic injury of the inner-ear labyrinth; chemical inflammation does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated mechanism.
Zellweger-spectrum metabolic and CNS disease; hepatic dysfunction and retinal disease commonly affect >=30%. Common hearing impairment omitted by cap; severity varies.
Autoimmune destruction of endocrine pancreatic beta cells causes insulin deficiency. Retinopathy, nephropathy and neuropathy are separately diagnosed complications.
Spondyloepiphyseal skeletal dysplasia with vertebral, epiphyseal and joint abnormalities; no established extraskeletal organ disease.
Gastrointestinal hamartomatous polyposis and characteristic mucocutaneous pigmentation define the syndrome; additional cancers are separate diseases or risks.
Defined by impaired voluntary gaze; neurologic involvement includes ataxia in 80-99% and developmental or cerebellar abnormalities in 30-79%.
Multiple impacted and supernumerary teeth; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Cranial suture fusion defines disease; aortic valve stenosis is reported in 1/2 patients, supporting cardiovascular involvement, although the sample is very small.
MYO6-related nonsyndromic progressive sensorineural hearing loss; the gene alone does not establish other organ involvement.
Chronic intestinal dysfunction defines this umbrella; no specific infectious, immune or metabolic cause applies across the group.
GRM6-related retinal signaling dysfunction causes congenital stationary night blindness; no separate CNS disease is established.
GI cytotoxicity and marrow failure define poisoning; acidosis 80-99% and cardiac injury 30-79%. Renal failure and encephalopathy, each 30-79%, omitted by cap.
Defining hypotrichosis and skin changes accompany lymphatic vascular malformation with lymphedema and telangiectasia; eyelash loss does not establish ocular damage.
